summary: Toshio Ando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1929–1932). He held posts at Otani University (~1949–1973) and Doho University.

Toshio Horiuchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Tokyo (~2003–2010). He held research posts at Toyo University (~2015) and Zhejiang University (~2019).

Toshio Nagahiro worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Kyoto University. He held positions at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities, Kyoto University, Kurokawa Institute of Ancient Cultures, and Kyoto Tachibana University.
Toshio Sako is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikidō Takasaki and Ekyo Ejima, and at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1977), Chuo University (~1977–1987), Tokyo Institute of Technology, and Hannan University.
Toshiya Unebe is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. By 2009, he served as Associate Professor of Indian Studies at Nagoya University.

Totsudo Kato was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under teachers including Seiran Ouchi, Enryo Inoue, and Banne Shimada, attending several institutions. He taught at Shakitoku Kyoko, Setagaya Gakuen, Komazawa University, Toyo University, and Nihon University.

Tou-hoi Fok was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at New Asia Institute, Otani University, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, where he also lectured from around 1972 to 1982.
Touraj Daryaee is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at UCLA (~1993–1999) and held a post at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who earned his degrees from Kyoto University. He taught at Otemon Gakuin University, served as professor at Osaka City University, and directed the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).

Travis L. Smith is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD at Columbia University. He held posts at Barnard College and the University of Florida (attested 2012).
Trent Walker is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt.

Trevor Leggett worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at King's College London, the University of London, and SOAS, and headed the BBC Japanese Service (~1946–1970) while regularly lecturing at The Buddhist Society.

Trijang Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Gyuto Monastery and under masters including Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo. He served as a teacher at Ganden Shartse Monastery and taught numerous prominent Buddhist figures.
Trinle Lhundrub studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tro Shul Khenpo Jampal Dorjé studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Troy Organ was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (~1939–1941). He held academic posts at Parsons College, Chatham University, the University of Akron, and Ohio University.

Trulshik Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under teachers such as Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and taught students including Tenzin Gyatso and Adam Pearcey.
Trung Huynh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of the West under doctoral supervisor Darui Long (attested 2016).

Trungram Gyaltrul is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute and earned a PhD from Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, later founding the United Trungram Buddhist Foundation and Fellowship.
